answers.d01: 同一个概率式 P(数据|假设)，问的问题不同，名字就不同。似然是固定看到的数据，比较不同假设：哪个假设让这批数据更可能出现？后验是看完数据后反过来问：哪个假设现在更可信？掷硬币10次出了9次正面。若硬币公平（正面率0.5），这个结果的概率约0.5¹⁰≈0.001；若正面率是0.9，概率≈0.9⁹×0.1≈0.039。后者的概率高，就说「正面率0.9」对这个数据的似然更大——注意这只是「它更能解释数据」，不等于「它更可信」。要算后验，还得乘上先验：一枚九成正面的怪硬币本来就极罕见，先验很小，乘起来之后公平硬币可能仍然更可信。一句话：似然是数据给假设打的分，后验是分数加上原有可信度之后的最终判断。
answers.d02: The average hides spread. Two classes both average 70: one where everyone scores 68-72, one ranging from 30 to 100. Same mean, very different classrooms. Population variance packs that spread into one number: take each value, subtract the mean, square it, then average those squares. For scores 68, 70, 72: deviations are -2, 0, 2; squares are 4, 0, 4; variance = 8/3 ≈ 2.7. Why square? Raw deviations always sum to zero—below-mean and above-mean values cancel—so we need something that ignores the sign. Squaring also punishes big misses: a value 10 off contributes 25 times more than one only 2 off, so variance is sensitive to outliers. Side effect: units get squared (points squared), so people usually report the square root, the standard deviation. Stretch the data twice as wide and variance grows fourfold.
answers.d03: 正反馈指的是：过程中一部分输出被送回输入，且方向相同，于是变化自己给自己加油。对着音箱旁的麦克风讲话，音箱放出的声音被话筒再拾入、再放大，几秒内变成刺耳啸叫——每循环一次都比上次更大。负反馈相反，像空调恒温：温度高了就制冷，把系统拉回原状；正反馈则把系统推离原状。但「正反馈」说的是方向，不是好坏。复利和口碑传播是正反馈：钱生钱、用户带用户，越滚越多，是好事；银行挤兑、瘟疫扩散也是正反馈：越恐慌越取钱，越传播越多人感染。同一个结构，结果取决于它放大的是什么。现实中放大总有尽头：音箱功率有限、市场会饱和，所以增长曲线后期总会放缓。
answers.d04: Opportunity cost is the value of the best thing you give up—not all the things you give up, just the best one. Your free afternoon has three options: a part-time shift worth 150 yuan, a gym session plus rest you'd value at 100, or a movie worth 60. If you take the shift, the opportunity cost is 100, because the gym was the best alternative you actually passed up; the movie does not add to the cost—it was never a contender. The point: even free choices cost something, because an hour spent one way cannot be spent another. So a choice is worth it only if its value beats the best alternative. Change the situation: if an exam is tomorrow, studying becomes the top alternative, and suddenly that movie is expensive. The real price of anything is what you would otherwise have done with the same time.
answers.d05: 「检测出阳性，到底有多可能真生病？」贝叶斯公式回答的正是这个问题：阳性的人里既有病人也有健康人，要看各占多少。设某病在人群中每万人有100个病人。化验对病人99%报阳性，约99人；对健康人有5%误报，9900×5%≈495人。阳性共约594人，其中真病人99人，所以阳性者患病概率≈99/594≈17%。写成公式：P(病|阳性)=P(阳性|病)×P(病)÷P(阳性)，分子是「病人且被测出」，分母是「所有报阳性的人」。关键在于：误报率虽只有5%，但健康人基数大得多，假阳性反而占多数。若病更罕见，同样的检测下阳性可信度更低。所以拿到阳性先别慌，要结合患病率换算。
answers.d06: A web page often reads data from a database, which is slowish, so the application keeps a fast copy—the cache—and serves later requests from it. The problem appears the moment the real data changes: the price is updated in the database, but the cache still holds the old one, and customers see stale prices. Cache invalidation is the discipline of deciding when a cached copy is no longer trustworthy and must be dropped or refreshed. The simple approach is a TTL: expire every entry after, say, 60 seconds—cheap, but stale for up to a minute. The careful approach is write-through: whenever the database is updated, also update or delete the cache entry—always fresh, but more code and more failure modes. Every web application lives somewhere on this scale between freshness, speed, and complexity; that is why cache invalidation is famously called one of the hard problems of computer science.
answers.d07: 冰淇淋销量和溺水人数同涨同跌，但吃冰淇淋不会让人淹死——背后是同一个原因：夏天。天热既让人多买冰淇淋，也让更多人下水，两个数字才一起上升。这种藏在背后的共同原因叫混杂因素，是「相关不等于因果」最常见的来源。要判断因果，得排除三种解释：纯属巧合、存在混杂因素、因果方向反了。一个实用的检验是固定混杂变量：只比较同样炎热的那些天，如果冰淇淋和溺水的关系消失了，说明两者之间多半没有直接因果。更可靠的是随机实验——随机把人分成吃与不吃两组，混杂因素就被拉平了。所以看到相关先追问一句：还有别的因素在同时推着这两件事吗？
answers.d08: Compound growth means growth on growth: each period's gain is added to the base, so the next gain is bigger. At 10% a year, 1,000 becomes 1,100, then 1,210, then 1,331—the yearly increase itself grows from 100 to 121 to 133. The formula is A = P(1+r)^t, and the exponent is the whole story: the same rate applied longer does not add, it multiplies. A handy rule of thumb: money doubles in about 72/r years, so 8% doubles in roughly 9 years. Why the starting amount matters: growth is multiplication, so everything scales by the principal—twice the starting money means twice the final amount, forever, at the same rate. And because time sits in the exponent, starting earlier usually beats saving more later: 1,000 invested 10 years sooner can outgrow 1,500 invested later.
answers.v01: 过拟合就是「把旧题背下来了，却没学会解题」。一个学生把历年试卷答案逐字背熟，模拟考（就是那些旧题）满分；换一套新题就垮，因为他记住的是题目本身，而不是规律。机器学习模型也一样：模型太灵活、数据又少时，它会把训练数据里的噪声和巧合也当成规律拟合进去，于是在训练数据上表现完美，遇到没见过的新数据就错得多。所以判断模型好不好，不能只看它在训练数据上的成绩，要看它在没见过的新数据上的成绩。办法也和「别死记硬背」一样：多给数据、让模型简单些、给它加约束，逼它只学规律、放过噪声。
answers.v02: Search for 'bayes' and the engine returns 10 documents, 8 of which are relevant. Unknown to you, the corpus actually contains 20 relevant documents. Two different scores come from this one experiment. Precision: of what we returned, how much was right? 8/10. It measures how clean the result list is. Recall: of everything relevant, how much did we find? 8/20. It measures how complete the search was. Now loosen the matching rules to return 30 documents covering all 20 relevant ones: recall jumps to 100%, but precision drops to 20/30—more noise in the list. Tighten the rules and precision rises while recall falls. Which to optimize depends on the task: a lawyer who must find every relevant document needs recall; a user scanning the first page of web results mostly needs precision.
answers.v03: 自然选择不需要动物「努力」，它是一个筛选过程。三个条件凑齐就会发生：个体有差异，差异能遗传，不同差异留下后代的数量不同。比如细菌里随机出现了个别耐药变异——注意，是在接触抗生素之前就随机产生的。用药后，绝大多数细菌被杀死，耐药的那几个活下来并繁殖，下一代种群里耐药菌比例大增。细菌没有「想」变强，是药物像筛子一样留下了碰巧合适的个体。所以不说「为了耐药而进化」，只说「耐药个体被留下了」。改变条件看看：停用抗生素后，如果耐药有代价（比如长得更慢），非耐药菌又会重新占上风。育种家用的是同一套机制，只是把「环境筛选」换成了「人的挑选」。
answers.v04: An operation is idempotent when doing it once and doing it many times leave the same result. SET status = 'paid' is idempotent; ADD 1 TO total is not. Distributed systems care because you can never be sure a request arrived: a payment call times out—did the server process it or not? The only safe move is to retry, and retrying a non-idempotent operation charges the customer twice. The standard fix is an idempotency key: the client generates a unique ID per logical operation and sends it with every retry; the server remembers which keys it has seen and returns the stored result for duplicates. Note it is a designed property, not an accident: HTTP GET and DELETE /items/42 are idempotent by contract, while POST /charge is not unless you build the key logic in. Rule of thumb: make every operation safe to replay.
answers.v05: 信息熵回答的是：平均而言，看到结果那一刻你有多「意外」。把这份意外算成一个数：H = −Σ p·log p，即每种结果的意外程度按其出现概率加权平均。抛一枚公平硬币，正反各半，H=1比特；如果正面概率是99%，你几乎总能猜对，结果很少带来新信息，H≈0.08；某个结果必然发生时H=0。均匀分布最不确定，道理很直观：各结果一样可能，你无法押注任何一个，看之前排除不了任何可能；一旦某结果概率偏高，你多少能预料它，不确定性就下降了。改变条件：把99%调成60%，熵回升；分布越接近对半，熵越高。迁移一下：均匀随机的密码最难猜，因为每种可能都得老老实实挨个试。
answers.v06: Two threads, two locks. Thread A locks the customer table, then needs the orders table. Thread B locks orders, then needs customer. Each holds one resource and waits for the other's; neither will release what it holds, so both wait forever. That is deadlock, and it requires four conditions at once: resources are exclusive, holders keep them while waiting for more, nothing can be forcibly taken back, and a cycle of waiting closes (A waits for B, B waits for A). Remove any one condition and deadlock becomes impossible. The practical fix: make every thread acquire locks in the same global order—then the cycle cannot close, because whoever holds orders never waits for customer while holding it. Alternatives are timeouts with rollback, or avoiding multiple locks. As systems grow and touch more shared resources, lock-order discipline is the cheapest insurance.
answers.v07: 公共物品有两个特征：非排他——没办法把没付钱的人挡在外面；非竞争——多一个人使用，不减少别人能用的量。路灯、国防、烟花表演都是：烟花在天上炸开，付没付费的人都看得见，多一个观众也毫不费力。麻烦随之而来：既然不花钱也能享受，每个人最划算的策略就是一分不掏、等着别人出钱，这就是搭便车。人人这么想，就没人出钱，结果公共物品供给严重不足——路灯不会由一家向路人收费的公司来建。所以现实里常用税收加政府来提供国防和路灯，用捐赠和基金会维持开源软件这类公共物品。改变条件看看：一旦加上排他性，比如付费频道能把没交钱的人挡在门外，它就不再是公共物品，市场就能正常供给了。
answers.v08: Little's law says L = λW. In a stable system, the average number of items inside (L) equals the arrival rate (λ, items per minute) times the average time each spends inside (W, minutes). Coffee shop: 10 customers arrive per minute and each stays 2 minutes, so on average 20 people are in the shop at any moment. It is bookkeeping: each arrival deposits presence for its whole stay, so total presence accumulates at rate λ and each unit lasts W. The law is powerful because it assumes almost nothing—no particular arrival pattern, no queue discipline—only stability (work arrives no faster than it leaves) and long-run averages. Use it to infer one quantity from the other two: if the shop feels crowded (L=20) and people stay 2 minutes, throughput must be 10 per minute. If waiting time W doubles while λ is fixed, congestion L doubles.
